strategy.summary: Reproduce the NaN-propagation bug in scipy.special.gammainc/gammaincc (and chdtr/chdtrc) by building SciPy at the buggy commit fee31bf8964d and running the PR's added NaN tests. On the buggy revision the parametrized cases with a=0.0, a=inf (gammainc) and a=inf with x=NaN (gammainc/gammaincc) return finite values instead of NaN, so the tests fail. On the fixed revision the early std::isnan checks in igam/igamc return NaN and all tests pass.

build_commands: git fetch origin && git checkout fee31bf8964d
pinned_because: numpy 2.0.0 is the version observed in issue#21317 system info; the era ceiling is numpy<=2.2 (era-inferred, numerically relevant), so 2.0.0 is kept as the observed value rather than the ceiling
cython pinned to the 3.0 line from the era ceiling cython<=3.0 (era-inferred; issue#21317 lists 3.0.10, which lies in this line)
pythran 0.16.1 is taken from the documented build dependency list in issue#21317 (documented version, no documented constraint)
openblas has no documented constraint and no era entry (unbounded); the miniforge-provided OpenBLAS pkg-config install is used unpinned and this choice is stated here, not inferred from evidence

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest scipy/special/tests/test_gammainc.py scipy/special/tests/test_basic.py -k "test_a_nan or test_x_nan or test_chi2_v_nan or test_chi2_x_nan or test_chi2c_v_nan or test_chi2c_x_nan" -q -p no:cacheprovider
strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/special/tests/test_gammainc.py::TestGammainc::test_a_nan and test_x_nan (and the gammaincc counterparts), plus scipy/special/tests/test_basic.py::test_chi2_v_nan, test_chi2_x_nan, test_chi2c_v_nan, test_chi2c_x_nan
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision fee31bf8964d the test run reports failures, including test_a_nan[0.0] and test_a_nan[inf] for gammainc (a=NaN with x=0 gives 0 and x=inf gives 1), test_x_nan[inf] for gammainc (x=NaN with a=inf gives 0), and the corresponding gammaincc and chdtr/chdtrc ids. On the fixed revision (the PR head containing the std::isnan early checks in igam and igamc) the same command reports all selected tests passing.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import numpy as np, scipy.special as s; print(s.gammainc(np.nan, [-np.inf,-1.,0.,1.,np.inf,np.nan])); print(s.gammainc([-np.inf,-1.,0.,1.,np.inf,np.nan], np.nan))"
risks: Platform mismatch: the environment records a Windows miniforge path (C:/Users/matth/miniforge3/envs/scipy-dev/Library) alongside a gcc 10.3.0 ld.bfd toolchain, which is a Linux/MinGW-style setup. The toolchain and OS actually used are not confirmed; the defect is in C++ scalar kernels and may behave differently under MSVC or MinGW NaN handling.

Compiler flags are not stated. If the build uses -ffast-math or similar, std::isnan checks may be optimised away and the buggy behaviour may not transition. Confirm build flags before trusting a pass on the fixed revision.

LAPACK status is not confirmed beyond NO_LAPACK= in the OpenBLAS configuration string. The igam/igamc kernels do not depend on BLAS, so this is expected not to affect the transition, but it is not verified.
OpenBLAS version is unbounded in the evidence and is not pinned; numerically_relevant is marked true in the context, though nothing links it to special-value handling.
The chdtrc out-of-domain fix referenced in the same PR is not fully specified. Its tests may fail or pass for reasons other than the NaN check, so a partial transition is possible.
The buggy and fixed revisions are assumed to be fee31bf8964d and its PR head; the exact fixed commit is not given in the context.
Pytest -k selection matches by name; if test names differ between revisions, the selection could be empty and yield a vacuous pass. Check the collected count is non-zero.
Subnormal and signed-zero handling beyond the -0.0 test inputs is not stated, so behaviour outside the listed inputs is unknown.
The finite outputs (0 and 1) at infinite arguments are observed buggy behaviour, not confirmed correct values. The fix mandates NaN only for NaN inputs.

oracle.reference_source: np.isnan assertions in the PR tests (test_gammainc.py test_a_nan/test_x_nan and test_basic.py chi2 NaN tests)
oracle.why: The PR tests assert NaN presence exactly via np.isnan, so no numeric tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The np.isnan assertion sees finite values (0.0 or 1.0) for the a=NaN, x in {0.0, inf} cases and for the x=NaN, a=inf case, so assert fails. The same applies to the chdtr/chdtrc cases that the issue reports as finite.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the early std::isnan(a) or std::isnan(x) return of quiet NaN in igam and igamc, every np.isnan assertion holds and all selected tests pass.
